+# LB-04 art direction: one being, one useful workspace
+**Status:** operator-review proposal; not visual acceptance and not implementation authorization for broad renderer changes.
+**Scope:** three semantic keyframes × wide and compact compositions.
+**Product:** official `frontend/`. The external GAG demo and `demoplan.png` are reference material, not the product source or operational data.
+## Decision this sheet asks for
+Review whether the proposed composition and movement feel like the same recognizable being while keeping actual work comfortable to read and control. In particular, approve or revise:
+1. The body-to-work-plane relationship in the six frames below.
+2. The restrained motion vocabulary and permission hold.
+3. Whether the proposed 56rem split-layout threshold is a useful starting hypothesis.

+No shader, anatomy, texture, palette or production choreography is accepted by this document. The supplied reference's tiny tilted windows are explanatory diagrams; production work must remain readable/selectable DOM, not miniature 3D text.
+## Direction in one sentence
+One continuous point-field organism directs attention through its spine to one legible work plane; the plane is a stable, recoverable part of the workspace, not a pop-up competing with the body.

+The 2030 quality should come from precise structure, depth, responsive behavior and cause-and-effect—not more glow, more panels, or perpetual animation. The organism may be expressive, but the software must stay calm and candid.
+## Shared visual rules

+- Preserve the established palette and protected texture/GLB assets. Use current project tokens and material inputs; do not introduce a parallel palette. The known anchors are cyan `#7bf5fb`, purple `#b06eff`, green `#54f0a0` and orange `#ff7e40`; existing semantic/status tokens still own status meaning.

+- Preserve a recognizable cortex silhouette and continuous visible spine. Nerves begin at real anatomical seats and terminate at the relevant workspace edge. One attended destination is brightest; other branches stay quiet and identifiable.

+- Keep readable work in ordinary crisp DOM text. It must support selection, keyboard focus, scrolling, editing and browser zoom. A 3D thumbnail may indicate relationship, never carry the only copy of content or status.

+- Keep one primary focal point. In rest it is the invitation/body; during work it is the attended surface and its connecting nerve; during permission it is the explicit decision. Do not animate all panes at once.
+- Retain existing typefaces and neutral ramp unless legibility evidence justifies a change. Maintain contrast and label states in words and shape, not color alone.

+- Keep shell/navigation controls subordinate but discoverable. Stop, permission actions, current task identity and connection truth must not be hidden behind a decorative surface or require a hover gesture.

+- The body may breathe at rest only when current presentation facts support a resting, connected state. No inferred backend activity, memory learning, model “thinking,” worker, verification or success may be conveyed by ambient movement.
+## Six keyframes

+Legend: `B` = recognizable body/point-field; `S` = stable DOM work surface; `I` = input/composer; `C` = connection between anatomical seat and surface; `controls` = existing shell/status/Stop controls. These are composition wireframes, not pixel-perfect mockups.
+### 1. Rest / first contact
+| Wide composition | Compact/mobile composition |
+| ```text
+│ controls / connection truth                                │
+│                 (quiet field)                              │
+│             I  “What would you like to do?”                 │
+│ No task surface yet; no fake progress or floating windows. │
+│ controls / status    │
+│ short invitation     │
+│ I  Ask / type…       │
+│ keyboard-safe dock   │

+| Give the body generous negative space. The composer sits on the body's intake/spinal axis without covering the silhouette. Keep the text entry, connection state and Stop access in the familiar shell. | Use a compact but clearly recognizable body above the invitation; preserve the full-width typing target. The composer follows the visual viewport and safe-area insets when the keyboard opens; it must not obscure focus or submitted text. |
+### 2. Working / showing admitted work
+| Wide composition | Compact/mobile composition |
+| ```text
+│ controls / task identity / honest activity                 │
+│  cortex → seat   │ S  readable active workspace         │  │
+│   other seats    │ content, focus and scroll stay stable│  │
+│ I / Stop remain reachable; secondary tasks stay named.    │
+│ controls / task      │
+│ B ─ C  (compact cue) │
+││ S  active work     ││
+││ readable, scrolls  ││
+││ without body drift ││
+│ I / Stop, keyboard   │
+│ and task switcher    │

+| Place the body to one side only while the content plane remains comfortable. A single nerve traces the current task's stable seat to the surface. Keep other work reachable through named task controls, not a swarm of tiny panels. | The body becomes a compact presence/attention region; the DOM surface owns the available reading area. Keep its identity, focus and scroll position through resize, interruptions and keyboard visibility. Provide direct, reachable navigation to other tasks. |
+### 3. Awaiting real permission
+| Wide composition | Compact/mobile composition |
+| ```text
+│ controls / connection truth                                │
+│  posture settles       │ S  Permission required          │ │
+│                        │ exact action + target + reason  │ │
+│                        │ [Allow] [Deny]  [Stop]          │ │
+│ task / connection    │
+│ B ── held C          │
+││ Permission required││
+││ action / target /  ││
+││ reason             ││
+││ [Allow] [Deny]     ││
+│ actions stay visible │

+| The organism holds at the nerve endpoint; no forward lunge, bloom burst, success cue or auto-dismiss. Keep the requested action, target and reason legible beside the actual decision controls. Server authorization remains decisive. | Use a stable, readable decision sheet with actions visible without hover. When space is short, prioritize the decision details and controls over body size; keep the organism recognizable in a compact header/edge cue. Respect keyboard, safe area and focus visibility. |
+### Responsive rule (hypothesis, not an accepted breakpoint)

+Use available container width rather than user-agent/device sniffing. Try the side-by-side composition only when the relevant workspace container can reserve approximately `20rem` for the body, `34rem` for readable work and `2rem` for their gap (`56rem` total). Below that, use the compact stack. Test reflow at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS pixels, plus browser zoom and enlarged text. Adjust from observed clipping, reading comfort and keyboard behavior; do not preserve the split merely because a viewport is labelled “desktop.”
+## Motion contract: movement follows evidence

+Timing values below are starting ranges for a prototype, not claims about current implementation or a universal “feel-good” rule. Direct feedback and semantic state update immediately; choreography may finish later and may be interrupted. Retarget from the current pose rather than queueing stale keyframes.
+| Event / state | Body and spatial motion | DOM/control behavior and interruption |

+| Initial local input / typing | One restrained attention orientation, about 120–220ms; no per-keystroke pulse or camera move. | Echo the user's text and focus immediately on the next paint. Never wait for body animation or a network response before showing the local input. |

+| Surface focus / task switch | Focus transition about 160–260ms; preserve the same surface and anatomical seat. | Change selected task/focus immediately; transitions cannot delay keyboard or touch activation. Rapid switches retarget from current pose. |

+| Admitted work / surface growth | One 250–450ms nerve-to-edge reveal tied to the actual materialization/admitted-work event. Keep all reveals on one timeline. | Render usable DOM content as soon as available; show the actual task/activity label. No timer-driven fake progress, invented worker, or “reasoning” shimmer. |

+| Permission pending | Ease into a stable hold, about 120–220ms; then motion stays quiet. No approach through the decision plane. | Show actual pending decision, request details and Allow/Deny/Stop controls immediately. Animation never grants permission, marks completion, changes target or dismisses the prompt. |

+| Verified result | A small return/settle cue only after the admitted verification result is `pass`; initial cue up to 250–400ms. | Announce and display verified status from the event, with a persistent textual receipt. A completed-but-unverified task remains explicitly unverified. |

+| Failure, refusal, stale, offline, degraded or Stop | Halt or settle to a distinct stable posture; do not play the ordinary success/reabsorption choreography. | Preserve draft, task and recovery controls. Show the actual failure/freshness/Stop state. “Stop requested” is not “workers terminated”; “offline” is not “resting.” |

+| Safe dismissal / reabsorption | Optional 200–400ms retraction only after safe dismissal; leave the task seat/history trace recoverable. | Never remove content being read/edited or discard unsaved work because an animation completed. Reduced motion or interruption yields the same recoverable result. |

+| Ambient rest | Optional very slow, small, non-semantic breath; no whole-scene drift, repeated bright pulses or attention-seeking orbit. | Provide one always-reachable global pause/stop control for ambient motion. It stops outside a genuinely connected/resting state and never indicates model activity. |
+### Reduced motion, input and visual alternatives

+- Honor the operating-system `prefers-reduced-motion` preference and provide an in-product motion control. In reduced mode, remove travel, camera movement, orbit, scaling and ambient breath. Keep the same anatomy, visible state, labels, focus, controls and content. State changes may appear directly or use a minimal non-spatial cue; never hide information with the animation.

+- Because ambient movement would start automatically alongside usable content, expose a global pause/stop mechanism that does not trap focus. For an animation running longer than five seconds in parallel with other content, target WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2 (Level A); the user setting and explicit control must actually stop the movement.
+- Motion is not required to understand task state. Use persistent text and existing semantic icon/shape/pattern alternatives. Do not rely on hue, glow, sound or trajectory alone.

+- Keyboard activation and focus feedback are direct. Pointer/touch transitions are interruptible. Respect browser zoom and system text scaling; avoid controls being obscured by a virtual keyboard or safe-area inset.

+- Target real-user Interaction to Next Paint (INP) at or below 200ms at the 75th percentile, measured separately for desktop and mobile; separately trace first paint and sustained frame pacing. This is a responsiveness target, not a promise that every GPU animation frame is under 200ms.
+## Event-to-appearance truth table
+The live product's `deriveBeingPresentation(BeingFacts)` remains the semantic authority. This sheet proposes visual expression; it does not create a second state machine.
+| Admitted fact / presentation | Allowed expression | Must not imply |
+| Connected, fresh, no task; genuinely resting | Calm recognizable body, invitation and optional ambient breath. | Background inference, new learning, or work merely because particles move. |
+| User text/input; attention `human` | Immediate visible draft and a small attention orientation. | Model has received, understood or started reasoning before the backend event says so. |

+| `streaming` / active admitted task; attention `workspace` | One stable task seat, connected nerve and truthful activity label. | A worker exists based on an illustrative branch, or progress based only on elapsed animation time. |

+| `approvalPending` / `awaiting-human`; attention `approval` | Held posture and a decision plane showing exact request details and available controls. | Approval by gesture, animation, focus, timeout or visual transition. |

+| `verification: pending` then `pass` or `fail` | Checking cue, then distinct verified-pass or failed result from the final fact. | Completion equals verification; green/success before the actual passing result. |

+| Stale, unavailable, disconnected or degraded coherence | Explicit freshness/connectivity label; held or reduced body activity; recovery affordance. | Rest, current state, or a fresh receipt inferred from absent events. |
+| Refused, failed, restored or rollback | Distinct labelled outcome and safe recovery path. | Success choreography or concealed failure. |

+| Stop requested / engaged / stopped | Immediate request acknowledgment, then the factual engaged/terminal state when available. | That every worker or side effect has terminated before evidence confirms it. |
+| Safe close with recoverable task/receipt | Quiet return to the same body and reachable named history/task seat. | Deletion, loss of draft, or a “death” metaphor that overstates data lifecycle. |

+Current source vocabulary includes `fresh | unverified | stale | degraded | stopped` coherence, `none | human | workspace | approval` attention, explicit mirror projection/status, task activity and verification states. Preserve the kernel's precedence, including permission, stale and the verified/unverified distinction. The source map and limits are recorded in [the acceptance ledger](LIVING_BEING_ACCEPTANCE_LEDGER_2026-09-24.md).
+## Evidence, acceptance and unresolved constraints
+This is a review artifact only. It earns no completion points and does not establish that the product currently behaves this way. LB-04 is accepted only after:
+1. The operator reviews the reference-based six-frame composition and motion direction.
+2. A moving prototype proves the three states and key interruptions in both wide and compact layouts.
+3. Human review can distinguish the critical states with motion disabled and without relying on color alone.
+4. Actual renderer and interaction evidence is collected on named desktop and physical mobile devices.

+The target operating systems are Android 17 and iOS 27.0 stable, per the product ledger; exact Android and iPhone models are user-confirmed **TBD**. No physical mobile acceptance is currently available. Keep device/browser/GPU and human-review gates open; a responsive emulator or this static sheet is not a substitute.

+The performance framing follows the web.dev INP guidance: a good INP target is ≤200ms at p75 and should be segmented by mobile/desktop; responsiveness includes input handling and presentation of the next frame. Reduced-motion behavior follows the system preference exposed by `prefers-reduced-motion`. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2 (Level A) covers automatically moving content that runs for more than five seconds alongside other content; SC 2.3.3 (Level AAA) says interaction-triggered animation can be disabled unless essential. This design aims to preserve information and task usability even when all non-essential travel motion is removed.
+## Research anchors

+- [W3C WAI — Understanding WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3: Animation from Interactions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions): interaction-triggered motion can be disabled unless essential; this proposal keeps status and controls complete without it.

+- [W3C WAI — Understanding WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2: Pause, Stop, Hide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide): automatically moving content lasting more than five seconds alongside other content needs a user mechanism to pause, stop or hide it; the global motion control is included for this reason.

+- [MDN — `prefers-reduced-motion`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/%40media/prefers-reduced-motion): detects the user/device request to remove, reduce or replace non-essential motion.

+- [web.dev — Optimize Interaction to Next Paint](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-inp): current good INP threshold, p75 segmentation and the input-delay/processing/presentation model used for the responsiveness gate.

+- Internal source of product semantics: [`semanticKernel.ts`](../../frontend/src/livingMirror/being/semanticKernel.ts), with runtime map and existing evidence limits in [`LIVING_BEING_ACCEPTANCE_LEDGER_2026-09-24.md`](LIVING_BEING_ACCEPTANCE_LEDGER_2026-09-24.md).
